newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds pared early gains to settle slightly higher after bearish comments on inflation from a U.S. central banker fanned fears of a U.S. interest rate rise, sending U.S. bonds lower late in the session.

The September French bond future touched a high of 124.06 soon after opening then drifted lower as Bunds failed to build on a positive start and as hopes of a test of the French bond future contract high at 124.10 fizzled out.
PIBOR contracts started well, lost their gains as the franc slipped from an overnight high of 3.4085 to 3.4166, then settled higher as dollar strength helped the franc regain its poise.

Bond future traders said the U.S. market was the main focus at the moment and that the bearish comments from Federal Reserve governor Janet Yellen had not helped ahead of the release of the Fed's Beige Book on Wednesday.
"We're in a wait-and-see sort of mode," said one Matif trader at a French bank.
Yellen said the U.S. economy was "in an inflationary danger zone" and that the labour market was "quite tight".
Traders said the franc had come under pressure from mark buying by German investors and talk that the Bank of France was replenishing its mark reserves after recent intervention.
The short end of the French curve outperformed on Tuesday, leading to a curve steepening of three basis points between five and 10-year government bonds.
Short-dated French bonds also fared better than their German counterparts. The two-year spread over German bonds narrowed five basis points while the five-year spread come in two basis points.

Some bond traders said that while the three billion franc 2008 bond issue by Sweden had been more successful than its French franc bond issue in January the spread of 17 basis points over OATs was too tight.
One trader said on the one hand it was too expensive and also that the amount was a little large for the 12-year area of the curve.
According to prices from Caisse des Depots et Consignations, joint lead manager with ABN Amro Hoare Govett, the spread over the 8.50 percent 2008 OAT had widened to 20.2 basis points late on Tuesday.

Analysts said the outcome of the meeting of French public service unions later on Tuesday would need to be monitored closely although significant concerted union unrest following the summer break had so far failed to materalise.
The Treasury announced it would sell 300 to 500 million Ecu of 1999 and 2006 government bonds at auction on Thursday.
